faq.q: How much does a boat charter cost for a stag weekend in Marbella?
faq.a: For a budget-friendly option, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 cost €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks, and VAT. For a larger group, the Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: How many people can join a stag boat trip in Marbella?
faq.a: Most of our yachts (Mangusta 80, Azimut 58, Ferretti 94, Canados 86) take up to 12 passengers. Smaller boats like the Dubhe (5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (5 pax) are ideal for intimate groups. The Lagoon 380 catamaran holds 10, and the Fairline Targa 12m holds 10 as well.

faq.q: What is included in the boat rental price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden costs – you just show up and enjoy.

faq.q: Can we bring our own alcohol on board?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring your own alcohol, but we already provide beer, white wine, cava, and soft drinks. If you want premium spirits or a specific brand, feel free to bring it – just let the skipper know in advance.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a stag boat trip in Marbella?
faq.a: May to September offers the best weather, with sea temperatures around 20-25°C and air temperatures 25-30°C. June and September are ideal – still warm but less crowded. Even in April and October, you can enjoy sunny days, though the water is cooler.

faq.q: Do we need a boating license to charter a boat?
faq.a: No, you don’t need a license. All our boats come with a professional skipper who handles navigation, safety, and mooring. You can relax and focus on the stag party – the skipper is there to ensure a smooth experience.

faq.q: Can we customise the itinerary for our stag weekend?
faq.a: Absolutely. While we provide a 3-day plan, you can adjust routes, stops, and durations. Want to spend more time at a beach club or add watersports? Just tell us and we’ll tailor the trip to your group’s preferences.

data.body_html:
Planning a stag weekend in Marbella? A boat itinerary is the ultimate way to celebrate – think sun-soaked decks, swim stops in hidden coves, and chilled cava as you cruise the Costa del Sol. This 3-day plan mixes partying with relaxation, using our fleet from Puerto Banús. You’ll hit the best spots – Cabopino, Estepona, Sotogrande – with concrete distances and times so you can organise the perfect trip.

Why a Boat Itinerary Works for a Stag Weekend

A boat charter turns a standard stag do into an unforgettable adventure. You get privacy, flexibility, and a moving party venue. With a licensed skipper, you don’t need boating experience – just turn up and enjoy. Plus, all charters include drinks and snacks, so you don’t have to worry about logistics.

Day 1: Puerto Banús to Cabopino – Beach Club Vibe

Start your stag weekend with a 10-nautical-mile cruise east from Puerto Banús to Cabopino. Depart at 11:00 to make the most of the day. The journey takes about 40 minutes at cruising speed. Anchor near Cabopino’s sandy beach, where you can swim, paddleboard, or just soak up the sun. For lunch, head to a beach club – there are several with day beds and music. Return to Puerto Banús by 17:00, giving you time to freshen up before a night out in the marina’s famous bars.

Day 2: Puerto Banús to Estepona – Cala del Faro Swim

On day two, head west to Estepona, a 12-nautical-mile trip that takes about 50 minutes. Stop at Cala del Faro, a secluded cove near the Estepona lighthouse – perfect for a refreshing swim in crystal-clear water. Continue to Estepona’s marina for a relaxed lunch at a chiringuito. The return trip is easy, and you’ll be back in Puerto Banús by early evening. This day balances partying with a touch of Andalusian charm.

Day 3: Puerto Banús to Sotogrande – Luxury Lunch

For the grand finale, cruise 20 nautical miles to Sotogrande, a luxury marina known for its upscale vibe. The journey takes about 1 hour 15 minutes. Anchor at Cala Cortés, a stunning beach with turquoise water – ideal for a final group swim. Lunch at a beachfront restaurant in Sotogrande, then slowly cruise back. This longer trip is perfect for a relaxed, memorable last day.

Which Boat Fits Your Stag Group?

Choose based on group size and budget. For up to 12 people, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a head-turner, starting at €4,719 for 4 hours with a free jet ski. If you want a more affordable option, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both 12.5m) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – perfect for up to 9-11 guests. For a unique experience, the Lagoon 380 catamaran (10 pax) offers stability and space. All depart from Puerto Banús.

Costs and Inclusions – No Hidden Extras

All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% IVA. That means the price you see is the price you pay. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the 8-hour rate is €2,299. The Mangusta 80 (including grey variant) is €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp – just ask.

Practical Tips for a Smooth Stag Weekend

  • Book in advance – especially in June-September, as boats sell out.
  • Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a change of clothes – the sun is strong.
  • Let the skipper know about any special requests (e.g., cake, decorations).
  • Consider a sunset charter on one evening – the light over La Concha is stunning.
  • Remember to bring cash for beach clubs or tips if you wish.
